❓ Frequently asked questions

Why are some conversions reciprocal?

L/100km measures consumption (fuel per distance), while mpg and km/L measure economy (distance per fuel). Converting between the two uses division: 30 mpg (US) = 235.214583 ÷ 30 = 7.84 L/100km.

What is the difference between US and UK mpg?

The US gallon is 3.78541 L while the imperial gallon is 4.54609 L, so the same car shows a ~20% higher number in UK mpg.

What is a good L/100km figure?

Roughly: under 6 is excellent, 6–8 is good, 8–10 is average, and above 12 is thirsty for a passenger car.
